caveats: Launch and landing are converted to UTC from the page's own zone labels (EDT = UTC-4, PDT = UTC-7); the conversion reproduces the page's printed mission duration to the second.
The abstract's maximum crew dose attributed to an SPE covers the SPEs during STS-28 and STS-34 together; it is not STS-34's own dose and is compared with nothing here.
A low-inclination orbit inside Earth's magnetosphere is a different radiation environment from interplanetary space or the surface of Mars: this record is history and context, not a dose basis.

data.use_note: The abstract's 30 microGy is the maximum crew dose attributed to an SPE over STS-28 and STS-34 together, as the abstract states; it is not STS-34's dose. LANDFALL compares it with nothing.

quotes.text: Since STS-26, three large solar events have occurred during Shuttle missions; a geomagnetic storm during STS-29 and solar particle events (SPEs) during STS-28 and -34.
The maximum dose to a crew attributed to an SPE was estimated to be 30 microGy (70 microSv).
dose from an SPE is strongly dependent on numerous factors such as orbit inclination, SPE start time, spectral parameters and geomagnetic field conditions
